TEM narrows the symmetry and the source assigns Cmcm using the CaTi2O4 prototype, but it does not refine target Mg/Al/O coordinates, so atom sites are not inferred. The lattice product differs slightly from the separately reported V0 because printed quantities are rounded.

This record describes the CaTi2O4-type product established by runs 3 and 4. It is distinct from the lower-pressure CaFe2O4-type run-2 phase. It remains a production published record because the equation, coefficients, construction states, and provenance are complete, but it must not be presented as a multi-point fit.

Parameter covariance is not supplied.

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Parameter provenance</summary>

- **Origin of the parameterization:** Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Experimental method; Table 1; Sections 3.2-3.3; Table 2; Figure 4.
- **Equation:** Section 3.3: Birch second-order finite-strain EOS with Eulerian strain and K0'=4.
- **V0:** Section 3.3 and Table 2: 240.3(4) A3 for the recovered CaTi2O4-type conventional cell, Z=4.
- **K0:** Section 3.3: 206(+/-3) GPa, calculated as the normalized pressure of the single in-situ run-4 state after holding the separately measured V0 fixed.
- **Implicit k0 prime:** Second-order Birch finite strain fixes K0'=4; it is assumed rather than fitted or stored as a BM2 parameter.
- **Construction states:** Recovered run-4 zero-pressure cell fixes V0; the in-situ run-4 cell at the mean post-heating pressure of 64.3 GPa then determines K0 algebraically. Run 3 establishes phase identity but has no usable in-situ volume. This is not a regression fit.
- **Uncertainties:** The source says bulk-modulus uncertainty is calculated from the difference between ruby- and Pt-derived post-heating pressures; no covariance or confidence convention is published.

</details>
